bio: A Bachelor candidate in Psychology at Deakin University, Yi Yang moved from China to pursue their academic goals in Australia. Through 8 years of experience as an international student in Australia, Yi has developed a clear understanding of the hurdles newcomers encounter. Mentoring on housing and academics is where Yi excels, combining personal storytelling with actionable advice that resonates with international students. Approachable and patient, Yi is dedicated to being the mentor they wished they had when they first arrived in Australia. They are particularly skilled at helping mentees manage the emotional side of relocation alongside the practical tasks of settling in.

A senior lecturer in Education at University of Newcastle, Dr. Beatriz Diaz has dedicated 13 years to both academic excellence and student mentorship. Their mentoring philosophy is grounded in the belief that academic success is inseparable from personal wellbeing and a sense of belonging. Their mentoring strengths lie in scholarships and networking, where they combine scholarly expertise with practical, career-relevant guidance. Coming from Argentina, they bring an important cross-cultural perspective that enriches every mentoring conversation. They hold regular open office hours and actively encourage students to reach out, believing that early guidance can change the entire trajectory of a student's career.

Having lived in Australia for 1 years after moving from Indonesia, Linh Ahmad knows firsthand how much preparation and support families need. Supporting their child through enrolment and settling in at Macquarie University gave Linh invaluable insight into the practical and emotional challenges families face during this transition. Linh is particularly valued for their guidance on finances and visa, two areas where misinformation and uncertainty can cause families significant stress. Known for their empathy and practical mindset, Linh is committed to ensuring no family has to navigate Australia's student landscape alone. Their calm, reassuring presence makes them an ideal mentor for families who feel overwhelmed by the volume of information they need to process.
